name: VIX roll yield capture
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Earning the VIX Futures Premium
caseLead: VIX futures frequently trade above the spot VIX, allowing short futures positions to earn a return if prices decline as contracts approach expiry. The premium persists because investors pay for protection against equity sell-offs and often hold it regardless of price, while few participants can absorb losses when volatility rises, and geopolitical and policy uncertainty keeps demand for protection high even when markets stay calm.
caseRest: Short VIX futures positions can suffer large losses when expected volatility rises sharply during an equity sell-off. When a sell-off begins, the futures curve can move from contango, where futures are priced above spot, to backwardation within days, so short positions lose on both the roll and the rise in spot volatility. Rehyn estimates that a single episode can remove several years of accumulated roll yield, which is why the largest drawdown is far bigger than the volatility of normal months suggests.
figNote: Each card shows the highest closing level of the VIX during the episode. The VIX measures the volatility that S&P 500 options price in for the next 30 days: it has averaged about 19 over the long run, while readings above 30 signal market stress.

events.title: US credit rating downgrade and euro debt fears
events.text: Standard and Poor's downgraded the US credit rating on 5 August 2011 while euro area debt concerns spread, and the VIX closed at 48 on 8 August. The strategy lost because the futures curve moved into backwardation, so short positions lost as spot volatility rose.

events.title: North Korea tensions lift the VIX briefly
events.text: Threats between the US and North Korea lifted the VIX by about 44% to a 16 close on 10 August 2017. The strategy gained because the VIX fell back close to its earlier level within weeks and the curve returned to contango.

events.title: Short volatility products collapse in one day
events.text: On 5 February 2018 the VIX more than doubled to a 37 close, its largest one-day rise on record, as funds that sold volatility had to buy futures back. The strategy lost because the rise wiped out many months of roll yield.

events.title: Covid turns into a global funding crisis
events.text: The March 2020 sell-off turned a health emergency into a global rush for cash, lifting the VIX to an 83 close on 16 March. The strategy suffered its worst loss because the curve inverted and the VIX stayed above 50 for weeks.

events.title: Bank of Japan rate rise unwinds yen trades
events.text: A Bank of Japan rate rise and weak US jobs data forced yen-funded trades to close, lifting the VIX to a 39 close on 5 August 2024. Results were mixed because short positions lost that day but recovered as the VIX fell below 20.

events.title: US tariffs drive the largest spike since 2020
events.text: US tariff announcements in April 2025 lifted the VIX to a 52 close on 8 April, its highest level since March 2020. The strategy lost because the VIX rose from about 21 to 52 within a week, before the stop level closed positions.

instrument: VIX futures; first and second month contracts; rolled gradually each day
rules: Short futures held only while the curve is in contango; exposure reduced as the VIX rises; no position when the curve is inverted; smaller size around central bank meetings
costs: Estimated futures commissions and bid-ask spreads deducted at each roll
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from curve roll-down to spike control

legs.purpose: Earns the roll-down of futures towards spot
Earns the steepest part of the curve
Limits losses in a volatility spike
Provides collateral and earns the cash rate

entry: First-month futures at least 3% above the VIX, with the curve in contango
size: Set to a 10% annualised volatility target and halved when the VIX closes above 25
exit: Position reduced as futures converge towards spot and closed 5 days before expiry
stop: All short positions closed if the VIX closes above 30
marketWatch: The slope of the VIX futures curve and the gap between implied and realised volatility are key indicators now. Scheduled central bank decisions, major trade announcements and geopolitical deadlines matter because they can lift near-term volatility before the curve has time to adjust. Rehyn also watches the size of positions in volatility products, since crowded short positions have tended to amplify spikes.

favourable.heading: Calm markets with a steep curve
favourable.text: A steep contango curve favours the strategy because each futures contract falls towards a lower spot level as expiry approaches. In 2017 the VIX averaged about 11, so short positions earned the roll almost every month.

favourable.heading: Geopolitical fear that fades quickly
favourable.text: Tensions that fade within days favour the strategy because volatility returns to its earlier level and the curve resumes its roll-down. After the North Korea threats in August 2017, the VIX fell back close to its earlier level within weeks.

favourable.heading: Policy support after market stress
favourable.text: Central bank or government support after stress favours the strategy because it lowers volatility and restores the premium in the curve. After the Bank of Japan rate rise in August 2024, the VIX fell from a 39 close to below 20 within a week.

adverse.heading: Sudden global sell-offs
adverse.text: A rapid fall in equities hurts the strategy because spot volatility jumps above the futures price and short positions lose on the move. In March 2020 the VIX rose from about 14 in mid-February to an 83 close on 16 March.

adverse.heading: Forced buying by volatility funds
adverse.text: Crowded short positions hurt the strategy when funds must buy futures back at the same time, which pushes prices higher regardless of the economic news. On 5 February 2018 the VIX more than doubled in one day, so losses came from forced buying rather than from the economy.

adverse.heading: Inverted curve during prolonged stress
adverse.text: A prolonged inversion of the curve hurts the strategy because it removes the roll yield and turns the daily roll into a cost. Throughout 2022 the curve repeatedly flattened as the war in Ukraine and rate rises kept volatility high.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, using VIX futures prices and the volatility-based exposure rules above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects the VIX and the slope of the futures curve, which are then applied to the strategy's short futures positions.
